target.pinning_note: scripts/mutillidae_e2e.sh:214-215 clones --depth 1 and resets hard to the moving default branch, so this commit is what HEAD happened to be on 2026-07-25, not a pin the tooling enforces.

vulnerability.description: Unparameterised string concatenation of a request parameter into a SELECT executed via mysqli::query.

source.note: Line 46 ($_POST) applies at security levels 2-5; line 50 ($_REQUEST) applies at levels 0-1 because $lProtectAgainstMethodTampering is false there.

propagation.code: $lQueryString = "SELECT * FROM accounts WHERE username='".$pUsername."' AND password='".$pPassword."'";

sink.note: The sink is the mysqli METHOD, not the procedural mysqli_query. padv/static/joern/query_sets.py already lists 'mysqli::query', so the intercept list can express it.

route.method_note: At security level 0 user-info.php sets $lFormMethod=GET and reads $_REQUEST, so GET carries the payload. Levels 2-5 force POST and $_POST.
route.direct_access_note: src/user-info.php cannot be requested directly: it depends on $SQLQueryHandler, which only index.php constructs (index.php:190).

preconditions.evidence: src/index.php:481-485 lists user-info.php in $lPagesRequiringAuthentication and redirects to login.php with 302 when $_SESSION['user_is_logged_in'] is false.
src/index.php:26-27 defaults $_SESSION['security-level'] to 0; at that level SQLQueryHandler::stopSQLInjection is false, so no escaping is applied.
The accounts table must exist; src/set-up-database.php:209-213 creates and seeds it.

intercept_matching.key_format: <lowercased class>::<lowercased function>, or <lowercased function> for free functions

morcilla_contract.response_payload_format: base64 of a JSON array of {function, file, line, args[]}
morcilla_contract.argument_encoding: strings are emitted with surrounding double quotes, so the canary appears inside args[0] as part of a quoted string
morcilla_contract.arg_truncation_signal: in-band: strings longer than 251 bytes get a trailing '...' inside args[]; there is no truncation header
morcilla_contract.expected_query_length_note: The SELECT is roughly 70 characters plus the canary, so it stays well under the 256-byte argument limit.

positive_control_contract.description: A run-specific canary placed in the username parameter must appear verbatim inside argument 0 of mysqli::query at MySQLHandler.php:229.

negative_control_contract.description: The identical flow with a benign username must produce the same call with no canary in argument 0.
